d:
So, you've become a Blacksmith. That's a great choice if you want to make sure your blades never dull.
I reckon I know someone that can help with that by teaching you how to craft a Sharpening Wheel. Bring one of these out at your camp and all the adventurers and rogues in the area will be lining up to hone their weapons.
c:
There you have it, you can now craft your very own Sharpening Wheel. Most folk don't care much for camps being set up in the center of town, so you'll need to head into the wilderness if you want to test it out.
Oh, and just remember, no camp is complete without a campfire. You'll need one of those before you start up your camp. Most cooks can teach you to make a fire. If you haven't already, you might want to check in with someone who can train you in the culinary arts to learn the basics.

d:
Auberdine is a humble place, adventurer. You will not hear its name spoken in the boughs of Darnassus. Most reference only what the Sundering took from us--the thriving cities of Ameth'Aran, Bashal'Aran, and... Lathar'Lazal.
Yet Auberdine remains in their shadow.
I would see our work here recognized. A new vessel connects us to the kingdom of Stormwind, bringing life and supplies to our shores. I beseech you join its next voyage, and bring this letter to a human called Baros Alexston.
Make our home known.
p:
I can smell the sea on you, friend!
What brings you to Stormwind?
c: Baros opens the letter and begins to read it, his smile fading.
human-male

I wish it was that easy to help, adventurer. I really do.
Should you choose to spend more time in our lands, you will find that many are without. Stormwind's coffers are not what they once were, and what remains is spread thin.
Give this reply to the elder the next time you see him. It's not what he's hoping for, but it's all I have to offer right now.
p: You have returned. What news comes from Stormwind?
c:
Sad news indeed. Still, I thank you for making the journey.
With neither Stormwind nor Darnassus coming to aid us, it seems that Auberdine's fate is our own to decide.

d:
The Gnarlpine furbolg would not turn on their ancient allies so readily. We must learn more of their plight.
Search their abandoned homes for totems. If any survived the chaos of their departure, their engravings may tell us more of what happened here.
You'll find their camps along the western edge of the glen, though the grell and grellkin may have scattered them beyond.
p: Don't worry about any larger totems you might find. I wouldn't know what to do with them if you found a way to get them!
c:
Oh, it's even worse than I thought.
These engravings tell us that the Gnarlpine began having nightmares of being wiped out by some great shadow. Before long, that fear turned to rage--and the shadow to their former elven friends. To be aware of your own mind slipping away from you...
Our only hope is that this may help us better understand what is happening on Teldrassil. Thank you for your aid, friend.

d:
You are born kaldorei--the children of the stars--and shall become a great priestess of our goddess Elune. Her grace may illuminate our strengths, helping our strikes hit true, or it may help conceal us just as the moon may eclipse the sun.
Our Long Vigil after the defense of Mount Hyjal has ended, and we have joined an Alliance of others--which you will meet in due time. For now, you are nestled in the boughs of Teldrassil.
Demonstrate Mother Moon's gifts, and bask in her blessings.
c: You have seen what our goddess provides. Use it well, and she will never forsake you.

d:
Fascinating, aren't they? This is the first time I have ever been privy to the secrets of abomination creation.
I have been studying these notes, and it appears we need a heart. A massive one!
I hear there is a thunder lizard there of impressive size called Stormheart, that patrols along the canyon edge in Thousand Needles. With a name like that it must have the perfect heart. I must have that heart!
Oh, also I suggest you bring friends. Stormheart isn't known for being docile.
p: Oh, you've returned in one piece! Pity, if you hadn't your bones and what's left of your flesh would have made excellent fodder for my tinkering.
c:
Excellent! I can hardly contain my excitement. Oh, and the heart still has electrical pulses? That's impressive. I won't have to shock it back to life then!
This heart will be a wonderful addition to the abomination, and certainly looks to be the specified size, if these notes are correct.
Ah, I love it when a plan comes together.
